name: Nagoya / Ghibli Park
days: 1 full day for Ghibli Park (together with friend, her must-see too), plus reconvene-day free time on arrival
overview: Ghibli Park is a must-do for both — full day dedicated to it, no split with Nagoya city time. No particular favorite film/area, wants to see everything, so this means targeting the Premium All-Access Pass over individual area tickets. On the reconvene day before Ghibli Park, there's likely free time before friend's flight lands — that window can be used for Nagoya city recommendations.

recommendations.title: Ghibli's Grand Warehouse
recommendations.summary: Largest indoor area, exhibition zones and film set recreations. ~3 hours.
recommendations.body: The largest indoor area, exhibition zones and film set recreations across multiple movies, plus a cinema showing original Ghibli shorts. Budget about 3 hours here alone.

recommendations.title: Hill of Youth
recommendations.summary: Antique shop from Whisper of the Heart, Cat Bureau from The Cat Returns.
recommendations.body: Features the antique shop from Whisper of the Heart and the Cat Bureau from The Cat Returns.

recommendations.title: Dondoko Forest
recommendations.summary: Satsuki & Mei's House from My Neighbor Totoro. Premium ticket required for interior.
recommendations.body: Includes Satsuki & Mei's House from My Neighbor Totoro — interior access requires the Premium ticket, not Standard.

recommendations.title: Mononoke Village
recommendations.summary: Themed area based on Princess Mononoke.
recommendations.body: One of the five themed areas at Ghibli Park.

recommendations.title: Valley of Witches
recommendations.summary: Newest area — Howl's Moving Castle, Okino Residence, Witch's House.
recommendations.body: The newest area, featuring Howl's Moving Castle, the Okino Residence, and the Witch's House — interior access also requires Premium.

recommendations.title: Ghibli Park ticket logistics
recommendations.summary: Time-sensitive — tickets release 2 months out, Premium pass recommended.
recommendations.body: Tickets release at 2pm JST on the 10th of the month, two months before the visit date. For a February 2026 visit, that's a December on-sale date. Since the goal is seeing everything, get the Premium All-Access Pass, not individual area tickets — Standard doesn't include interior access to Satsuki & Mei's House or the Howl's Castle buildings, and there's no day-of upgrade. International visitors use the official overseas purchase page, which has fewer time slots than the domestic version — book within the first 15-30 minutes of sales opening. Passport number required at booking; passport shown at the gate. This is the one piece of the whole trip worth locking in early, since tickets sell out fast.

recommendations.title: Expo 2005 Aichi Commemorative Park (Moricoro Park)
recommendations.summary: The forested grounds surrounding Ghibli Park itself.
recommendations.body: Ghibli Park sits inside this larger park, which has forested walking paths, gardens, and a satoyama (traditional rural landscape) area — free to enter even without a Ghibli Park ticket. Given the day is fully dedicated to Ghibli Park, this is more of an ambient note than a separate stop.

recommendations.title: Atsuta Shrine
recommendations.summary: Major shrine with old-growth forest grounds — best pick for the reconvene-day window.
recommendations.body: One of Shinto's most important shrines, said to house one of Japan's three sacred imperial treasures. Quieter and less touristed than the Kyoto/Nara shrines already on the itinerary, with heavily forested old-growth grounds — hits both traditional-sites and nature interests in one stop. Easy to cut short or leave whenever friend's flight status firms up, unlike something with a fixed showtime.

recommendations.title: Osu Shopping Street
recommendations.summary: Nagoya's international food district — best bet for vegetarian options.
recommendations.body: Nagoya's signature dishes (miso katsu, tebasaki wings, hitsumabushi eel) are all meat/fish, not vegetarian-friendly by default. Osu Shopping Street is the reliable vegetarian option — home to halal grocers and a growing cluster of Indian, Nepali, and Middle Eastern kitchens. Also doubles as a retro/subculture shopping district (vintage, anime, electronics), some overlap with the Akihabara/Nakano Broadway pull noted for Tokyo.

recommendations.title: Nagoya Castle
recommendations.summary: Major castle (largely reconstructed), if a second castle stop fits.
recommendations.body: One of Japan's major castles, though largely a reconstruction (the original keep was lost in WWII). Recall Matsuyama Castle is already "if convenient" elsewhere on the trip, so this would be a second castle option, not necessarily both. Surrounding grounds have a moat and garden areas, similar to Osaka Castle Park.
